scope: Plan state for saivage-v3 analyst-as-control-surface migration Stage 000, focusing on repeated no-probe/no-git operator-wait heartbeat escalations and the unresolved Node runtime blocker. Inspected non-secret plan state, immutable Stage 000/protocol documents, prior inspection reports, and plan-history summaries. executive_summary: Stage 000 remains externally blocked: the last authorized fresh evidence carried through heartbeat 39 is Node v24.15.0 while the project requires Node >=22.12.0 <23. Given the current empty plan queue and no external/operator signal of a runtime fix, the compliant Planner action is to hold with no pending stage; dispatching more heartbeats is compliant only as a status artifact but is not required by PROTOCOL-r4 and has already become a no-information loop.

questions_answered.question: 1. Given the project objectives and recent history, is there any compliant action the Planner can take other than repeated strict operator-wait heartbeat stages while no external/operator signal confirms Node >=22.12.0 <23?
questions_answered.answer: Yes: the Planner can and should keep the plan quiescent with current_stage_id null and stages [] while reporting the operator-required action. That is more compliant and less noisy than repeating heartbeat stages. It must not seed a fresh prerequisite retry or advance to Stage 001 until external/operator evidence says Node >=22.12.0 <23 is active. Repeated strict no-probe/no-git heartbeats have been accepted historically, but they do not advance Stage 000 and are not required by the stage publication protocol.

questions_answered.question: 2. Would dispatching another heartbeat using only the latest summary remain compliant, or does the plan protocol require holding with an empty queue pending operator signal?
questions_answered.answer: A strict no-probe/no-git heartbeat that uses only the latest summary would remain within the same constraints that heartbeats 24-39 followed, provided it performs no shell/git/MCP git/runtime probes/validation/product edits/fresh retry seeding. However, PROTOCOL-r4 does not require such heartbeats. Its consumer rules say the queue is scanned when empty and new published stages are appended by name; it does not define periodic wait-heartbeat stages. The better plan-state representation is the current empty queue pending operator signal.

questions_answered.question: 3. Is it permissible to seed a fresh Stage 000 prerequisite retry without an external/operator signal, or would that violate the no-probe/no-retry constraints recorded in recent escalations?
questions_answered.answer: It is not permissible under the recorded constraints. Recent summaries explicitly carry the last authorized fresh retry evidence (Node v24.15.0) and say to hold until an external/operator signal states Node >=22.12.0 <23 is active, then seed a fresh Stage 000 prerequisite retry. Seeding a fresh retry now would necessarily invite another Node/prerequisite probe without new evidence and would repeat the no-probe/no-retry violation pattern identified in prior inspection inspect-stage000-node-blocker-loop-policy-20260525.

questions_answered.question: 4. What exact next stage, if any, should be added to the plan now?
questions_answered.answer: None now. Leave /work/saivage-v3/.saivage/plan.json as current_stage_id null and stages []. After an explicit operator signal confirms Node >=22.12.0 <23 is active for /work/saivage-v3, add exactly one fresh Stage 000 prerequisite retry using the next unused retry id following the existing convention: 000-breakage-detection-harness-fresh-retry-after-node-runtime-fixed-40 (or, if the Planner maintains a separate fresh-retry counter rather than global Stage 000 suffixes, the next unused fresh-retry id in that counter). Do not add Stage 001 until Stage 000 closes.

findings.title: The current empty queue is the correct compliant hold state; protocol does not require heartbeat stages
evidence: /work/saivage-v3/.saivage/plan.json lines 2-4 show updated_at 2026-05-25T05:30:19.967Z, current_stage_id null, and stages [].

PROTOCOL-r4 consumer rules lines 55-59 state that the consumer scans for new stages when its queue empties, sorts new stage directories by name, and appends them to the queue; no rule requires synthetic wait or heartbeat stages while externally blocked.

Prior inspection inspect-stage000-node-blocker-loop-policy-20260525 concluded that no pending stage with archived escalation/hold evidence best represents an operator hold and prevents automatic retry loops.
findings.root_cause: A blocked external prerequisite is not executable work. Heartbeats are bookkeeping/status artifacts, not a protocol-mandated queue item.
findings.impact: Leaving the queue empty prevents unnecessary Manager dispatches and avoids expanding plan history with repeated no-information escalations.

findings.title: Another heartbeat would be narrowly compliant but low-value if it strictly avoids probes and git
evidence: History entries 24-39 repeatedly state strict no-git/no-probe heartbeats were accepted when they used only the prior summary, wrote only permitted .saivage stage-local artifacts, and avoided shell, git/MCP git, validation, runtime probes, product/harness/immutable edits, and fresh retry seeding.
Heartbeat 23 was rejected because the Coder report stated MCP git_commit was attempted, demonstrating that even bookkeeping heartbeats have a real prohibited-action risk.
The last five recent histories in the request and the plan-history extraction all repeat the same conclusion: hold until external/operator signal states Node >=22.12.0 <23 is active.
findings.root_cause: The heartbeat mechanism has become a liveness/status loop around an unchanged external blocker. It can comply only by intentionally not gathering fresh evidence, which also means it cannot change the decision state.
findings.impact: Further heartbeats consume agents and increase the chance of another prohibited-action mistake without improving the Planner's information.

findings.title: A fresh Stage 000 retry before operator signal would violate the recorded no-probe/no-retry hold constraints
evidence: Heartbeat summaries 35-39 all end with the same condition: hold until external/operator signal states Node >=22.12.0 <23 is active, then seed a fresh Stage 000 prerequisite retry.

Prior inspection inspect-stage000-node-blocker-loop-policy-20260525 finding F2 found that repeated immediate fresh retries after no-probe holds conflicted with no-probe operator-hold intent absent evidence of Node repair.
Stage 000 cannot close without running prerequisite and validation commands, so any fresh retry would be a new probe rather than a prior-summary-only heartbeat.
findings.root_cause: Fresh retry semantics require checking the runtime/prerequisites. Without an intervening operator-fix event, that repeats the same unauthorized probe of the known Node blocker.
findings.impact: Would restart the loop, likely escalate on the same Node v24.15.0 evidence, and undermine the explicit operator-wait boundary.

evidence: Published stage directories currently visible are 000-breakage-detection-harness, 001-real-llm-analyst-resolver, and 002-tool-surface-alignment.

findings.impact: Seeding Stage 001 now would skip the foundational breakage-detection harness and compromise validation for all later migration stages.
